headline: German authorities are investigating what appears to have been an attempted explosive drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport after a drone carrying an explosive device was discovered near Ukrainian cargo aircraft, according to BILD. BILD reports the drone was found late Tuesday night on the airport apron with an attached package that security authorities identified as containing explosive material after a positive nitrate test. An X-ray reportedly revealed a detonator, but investigators believe it malfunctioned, preventing the device from detonating. The explosive package has been preserved for forensic examination rather than destroyed, and BILD reports NATO investigators are expected to participate in the investigation. The incident occurred near several Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft at one of Europe's most important cargo hubs, including shipments supporting Ukraine. Airport operations were temporarily suspended following the discovery. BILD also reports that shortly after the airport was closed, a DHL cargo aircraft aborted its landing and later struck an unidentified object approximately 400 meters above the ground and about six kilometers from the airport. The aircraft landed safely in Hanover, where damage to its nose section was discovered. German authorities have confirmed the collision occurred and are investigating it as a state security matter, though they have not publicly confirmed that the object was a drone or linked it to the explosive device.

headline: Officials with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) are reviewing an air-traffic safety incident Tuesday over Washington, involving Marine One while it was transporting President Donald J. Trump from the White House to Joint Base Andrews in Maryland. According to people familiar with the matter who spoke to The Washington Post, on Tuesday afternoon, Marine One, a military helicopter used to transport the President, took off from the White House, but air-traffic controllers hadn’t yet halted commercial flights at nearby Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport as required under safety protocols, in place since the deadly midair collision over the Potomac on January 29, 2025. During the incident, Marine One and a commercial jet taking off from Ronald Reagan didn’t appear to get dangerously close under federal rules and weren’t converging, indicating the incident didn’t amount to a serious close call, according to a Spokesperson with the FAA. “Marine One flights are piloted by some of the best aviators in the world, and at no point was the President in harm’s way,” said White House Spokesman Kush Desai.

headline: The U.S., Iran, and Oman are reportedly nearing an interim agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with the Trump administration aiming to announce a deal as soon as Wednesday, according to Axios. The reported framework would establish a 60 day arrangement under which inbound commercial shipping would transit through Iranian waters, outbound traffic would use Omani waters in coordination with Iran, no transit fees would be charged, and both sides would work to clear naval mines from the strait's median shipping lane before negotiating a permanent agreement. If finalized, the deal would mark a significant shift from pre-war arrangements by giving Iran a formal role in managing commercial traffic through the world's most important oil chokepoint. It would also likely preserve the ceasefire, reopen the door to broader U.S.-Iran negotiations, and avert the large scale U.S. military strikes President Trump has repeatedly threatened in recent days. According to Axios, the agreement was mediated by Oman with support from Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan, while U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff held direct discussions with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in recent days.

headline: The Trump administration has increased U.S. intelligence assets in Cuba as it intensifies pressure on Havana's communist government, according to POLITICO. Citing two sources familiar with the effort, POLITICO reports the U.S. has expanded its intelligence presence on the island in recent months, with one source saying the increased collection could support a range of future options, from intensified intelligence operations to potential military planning. The report does not indicate that a military operation has been approved or is imminent. The increased focus has also been partially visible in open source flight tracking. Over the past several months, the U.S. has conducted a noticeable increase in U.S. Air Force RC-135 "Rivet Joint" signals intelligence missions and U.S. Navy MQ-4C "Triton" high altitude ISR flights operating in the vicinity of Cuba, reflecting a broader increase in intelligence collection around the island. The move comes alongside a broader campaign by the Trump administration that includes an energy blockade, expanded diplomatic and legal pressure, and increased public messaging targeting the Cuban government. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has made Cuba a top foreign policy priority, while administration officials continue to say President Trump prefers diplomacy but is seeking fundamental changes from the regime.

headline: Iran is weighing a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz through a voluntary fund financed by Gulf states and European countries that depend on the route. Modeled on the Strait of Malacca system, the fund would cover navigation, environmental protection, and search-and-rescue rather than formal tolls. Backed by Oman, the proposal offers a legal workaround since international law bars mandatory transit fees in key chokepoints. - The Telegraph
